newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis end day up 1/4-plus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis end day up 1/4-plus.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended the day up more than 1/4 point, with most deals repriced to lower yields as munis avoided the downside in the U.S. Treasury market.
All of the large deals slated for sale Wednesday were priced before the 12-year Treasury auction.
A poor reception for Treasury's sale of $12 billion 10-year notes poured cold water on the market. The spillover may be felt on Thursday when the Treasury auctions $10 billion of 30-year bonds.

And market players are also bracing for retail sales data on Thursday. In a Reuters poll, economists expected overall retail sales to jump 0.7 percent in January versus 0.6 percent the previous month.
One trader said the market was up more prior to auction, but fell off after the auction.
An analyst said high grade bonds were improved by two to three basis points. And dollar bonds were up 1/4 tp 3/8.
"There was light to moderate activity," the analyst said. "The overall market is up 1/4 plus."

"New issue bidding was very strong on Tuesday and today it was firm to strong and that is what is making our market," he said. The overall tone of market is good, he noted, although the secondary market is not able to take advantage of it.
"We have had two days of a really strong to solid market," the analyst said, because demand for bonds is firmer and supply -- or the lack thereof -- is helping to firm market."
In the new issue municipal market, Smith Barney Inc priced and repriced Harris County Health Facilities Development Corp, Texas's $268 million Memorial Hospital System bonds.
The firm lowered yields in several maturities at the repricing, but left the top yield in 2024 unchanged at 5.77 percent.
Competitive pricings included Knox County, Tenn.'s $70 million general obligation bond deal, won by Morgan Keegan & Co at a true interest cost of 5.24 percent.
The firm reoffered 2017 bonds at a 5.50 percent yield.

In the futures market, the March municipal contract was up 4/32 at 116-8/32, while March Treasury bond futures fell 2/32 to 112-13/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts was 123 ticks, compared to 117 ticks at the close on Tuesday.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond, meanwhile, was unchanged 97-11/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
